tum ] illa est quam sequuntur apud nos docti, & quæ Græ-

page.notes: Arabic lines at the head of the column are copied from a low-resolution scan; the words marked [?] (including the Arabic on the first line and the name Mahmud, and the Arabic gloss فارقليط) are uncertain. "Hi-rami" may carry an accent over the final i. The hyphenated line-end breaks (Græ-corum, se-ctarum, occi-dentaliores, senio-rum, tradu-ctam) are read from the scan; the printed letters at the break are partly obscured. "Alsannabio" is printed with a long-s-like letter, transcribed with plain s. Margin note "Ib. l. 4." is read as "Ib." with some doubt. The paragraph beginning "In Evangelio" is a continuation from the printed dash at its start, which is kept as an italic opening.
